title: Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
summary: Given a binary tree with unique node values and an initial infection starting at a specified node, determine the total time required for the infection to spread to all nodes.
statement: Given a binary tree with unique node values and an initial infection starting at a specified node, determine the total time required for the infection to spread to all nodes.
constraints: The binary tree has 1 through 100000 nodes with unique integer values, and start occurs exactly once.
At minute zero start is infected; each minute infection crosses every parent-child edge from infected nodes.
Return the first minute when all nodes are infected.

hints: Infection can move both down to children and up to a parent.
Convert the tree into an undirected adjacency map, then run breadth-first layers from start.
Each completed frontier corresponds to one elapsed minute; stop after the last nonempty layer.
BFS distance is infection time, so the maximum layer distance is exactly the time to reach every node.
